newsitem.title: CHINA: China calls for halt to bullying of farmers.
newsitem.headline: China calls for halt to bullying of farmers.

text.p: China's State Council, or cabinet, has called for a crackdown on local officials who use heavy-handed tactics to force farmers to pay illegal fees and taxes, the Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.
"Some ... departments across China have seriously violated the interests of farmers by collecting illicit fees, illegal fund-raising, and the imposition of arbitrary fines and quotas," Xinhua said.

"The State Council has ... ordered any activity that might increase the burden on farmers be stopped, and any serious incidents and cases, especially those causing casualties, be avoided," Xinhua said.
Vice-premier Jiang Chunyun warned of punishment for local officials who ignored farmers' pleas for an easing of the burden of fees or who used heavy-handed tactics to bully farmers.
"Those who neglect the appeals, and even retaliate against farmers, must be seriously punished," Xinhua quoted Jiang as saying.

Local officials must strictly abide by rules laid down by Beijing on the collection of fees for rural communal funds and should give farmers a greater role in the collection, management and use of such funds, Jiang said.
Fees for communal funds should be capped at five percent of farmers' average net income, Jiang said.
"Any illicit charging of service fees, or illegal fund-raising and price increases, and any imposition of arbitrary fines and quotas, must be strictly banned," he said.
Jiang said illicit fees were still a major burden on Chinese farmers, whose incomes have in recent years risen much more slowly than than those of urban residents.
China's farmers, who account for 80 percent of the total population of 1.2 billion, earned an average of 1,578 yuan ($190) last year, compared with 5,059 yuan for city dwellers.
